claims.text: NO TASK WITHOUT EVIDENCE: Every candidate carries three things and is refused without them: reason, score, evidence. _candidate enforces this: a candidate with an empty reason or empty evidence raises rather than entering the queue.
claims.why: Function _candidate is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify enforcement.

claims.text: score = BAND + offset. The BAND (SOURCE_BANDS) is the source's priority. It is a PRIOR, chosen by a human, not a measurement.
claims.why: Score computation not implemented in this chunk; offset property is incomplete.

claims.text: The OFFSET, within [0, BAND_SPAN], is the measurement: test counts and entrypoint counts for inventory features, recall shortfall for eval misses, normalised churn x complexity for hotspots.
claims.why: Offset calculation not present; BAND_SPAN constant is defined but offset property is a stub.

claims.text: Once a candidate has been ATTEMPTED, the ledger's record of how that attempt ended puts a CEILING on its offset (OUTCOME_POLICY).
claims.why: OUTCOME_POLICY not defined in this chunk; ledger and ceiling logic absent.

claims.text: Cross-band comparison is therefore NOT a claim that one island beats one hotspot on evidence. It is the stated priority order.
claims.why: Ranking logic not present; BAND_SPAN is defined but comparison not implemented.

claims.text: Sources that require a fresh eval run or a whole-repo structural index are OFF unless asked for (--eval, --hotspots). The default queue is built from files already on disk.
claims.why: Queue building logic not in this chunk; CLI flags not defined.

claims.text: main can run at most ONE attempt (--once), and an attempt produces inert bytes (see daedalus.spine.attempt.PatchArtifact).
claims.why: main function not defined; PatchArtifact not in this file.

claims.text: There is no --apply, and adding one belongs in a different module with a different review.
claims.why: No CLI handling in this chunk.

claims.text: BAND_SPAN is kept strictly smaller than the gap between bands so a measurement can never silently reorder the stated priority -- not even into a TIE that the sort's own tie-break would then have to settle. A test pins this inequality.
claims.why: BAND_SPAN=50.0 is defined; band gaps in SOURCE_BANDS are at least 100.0 (e.g., 900-800=100), so BAND_SPAN < gap holds. Test presence uncheckable.

claims.text: EXIT codes: 0 means, and only ever means, a gated candidate exists.
claims.why: EXIT_CANDIDATE=0 is defined; comment states its meaning.

claims.text: EXIT_NO_CHANGE (2) and EXIT_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (3) are distinct facts.
claims.why: Both constants are defined with distinct values.

claims.text: EXIT_BY_STATE maps 'clean' to EXIT_CANDIDATE and 'no_change' to EXIT_NO_CHANGE.

_strs: Hand-maintained JSON does not have a schema checker standing behind it, so every list-shaped field is read defensively: a string where a list was expected is a typo, not a reason to drop a real work item.
claims.why: Function handles None, string, list/tuple, and returns empty tuple for None/empty string; matches defensive description.

claims.text: Candidate.evidence is the audit trail: it names the file the numbers came from and carries the numbers themselves, so a human reading the review packet can re-derive the score without re-running the picker.
claims.why: Candidate has 'evidence' field of type Mapping[str, Any]; docstring describes its purpose.

observations.what: Candidate.band property uses SOURCE_BANDS.get(self.source, 0.0) which returns 0.0 for unknown sources; but SOURCE_BANDS has no entry for 0.0, so unknown sources get band 0.0.
Candidate.offset property is defined but not yet implemented; it is a stub (no body shown).
SOURCE_BANDS keys include 'docref' but SOURCE_ORDER tuple does not include 'docref'; display order may omit it.
EXIT_BY_STATE only maps 'clean' and 'no_change'; other states like 'failed' are not mapped.
The module docstring claims 'NO TASK WITHOUT EVIDENCE' enforced by _candidate, but _candidate is not defined in this chunk.
The module docstring claims 'score = BAND + offset' but offset property is a stub; score is not computed here.
